verses.t: At one time the Buddha was staying at Sāvatthī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Monastery. At that time the monks from the group of six were swaying and tilting their heads while sitting in inhabited areas. … One should not sway one’s head while sitting in an inhabited area; one should sit keeping one’s head straight. If a monk, out of disrespect, sways and tilts his head while sitting in an inhabited area, he commits an offense of wrong conduct. if it is unintentional; if he is not mindful; if he does not know; if he is sick; if he has entered his dwelling; if there is an emergency; if he is insane; if he is the first offender. The tenth training rule is finished. The second subchapter on laughing loudly is finished.
“‘I will not sway my head while sitting in inhabited areas,’ this is how you should train.”
